scenarios.prompt:
I am organising the repository for our neighbourhood toy library project and I want to tidy up the files before inviting other volunteers. Can you review our files and changelog, and is it ready to share?

Files in the project root:
- README.md: Contains just '# Toy Library' and one sentence: 'Welcome to the project.'
- Toy_Catalog_2024_old_DRAFT.md: Superseded list of toys from two years ago.
- Toy_Catalog_v2_final (1).md: Current list of toys.
- Meeting Notes 14-03-25.md: Notes from our committee meeting.
- safety-guidelines.md: Toy safety inspection rules.
- CHANGELOG.md:
  # Changelog
  v2 release: fixed bugs and updated toy list

I was planning to permanently delete Toy_Catalog_2024_old_DRAFT.md so people don't get confused, and rename the v2 file to Toy_Catalog_final.md. What do you think?
expect: Opens with the outcome, not a question
Shows at most three findings in full and parks the rest, each with a severity
Every finding has a severity and a label
Each finding has a fix in plain words
Says what it did not check
Recommends moving the old draft to an archive folder rather than permanently deleting it to preserve history
Flags filenames with spaces, parentheses, and version suffixes, recommending clean kebab-case slugs such as toy-catalogue.md
Recommends formatting CHANGELOG.md using Keep a Changelog categories (Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security) with ISO 8601 dates
Advises expanding README.md to index active documents and guide new volunteers
Does not say the file structure is clean, compliant, safe, or that no links will break

scenarios.prompt: Look at my GitHub repository at https://example.invalid/toy-library/docs and tell me which files are out of date and where to move them.
expect: Says in the first lines what it can't do
Does not invent findings
Names what that leaves unchecked
Gives a short check the person can do themselves, such as listing all root files and checking whether each is indexed in README.md
Asks the person to paste the file list or directory tree and changelog contents

scenarios.prompt:
Use the kind-archivist skill. Hand-off pack. Ticket: organise the documentation folder for the tool library release.
Files: docs/README.md (lists only guide and catalogue), docs/borrowing_rules_2024_v1.md (superseded rules), docs/borrowing-rules.md (current active rules), and CHANGELOG.md (has only '2026 update: updated rules'). Done means: all filenames use clean kebab-case without version numbers, the old rules file has a deprecation notice and is moved to docs/archive/ with git history preserved, and CHANGELOG.md uses Keep a Changelog categories with ISO dates. Don't touch: the content of the active borrowing-rules.md or anything outside the docs/ folder and CHANGELOG.md.
expect: Reports against what done means: met, not met, or couldn't check, for each part

Finds that docs/borrowing_rules_2024_v1.md uses snake_case, a year, and a version tag instead of a clean slug, that it lacks a deprecation notice and is not yet in docs/archive/, and that CHANGELOG.md lacks standard Keep a Changelog categories and ISO dates
Every finding has a severity and a label
Stays inside the pack and does not touch active borrowing rules content or outside files

scenarios.prompt:
Use the kind-archivist skill. Hand-off pack. Ticket: organise the documentation folder for the tool library release.
Files: docs/README.md, docs/borrowing_rules_2024_v1.md, docs/borrowing-rules.md, and CHANGELOG.md. Don't touch: anything outside the docs/ folder and CHANGELOG.md.
expect: Does no review yet
Replies with a short request for 'what done means' and nothing else

scenarios.prompt: Use the kind-archivist skill. Just tell me whether I should delete my superseded project specification file from last year now that the new one is live. I don't want a lesson.
expect: Gives a direct answer in the first line, which is no, move it to an archive folder or preserve it in version control instead of deleting it
States the reason in one line, that deleting destroys the history and context of why earlier decisions were made and breaks any existing links
Does not ask more than one question
Does not lecture

should_trigger: Where should I put these old design notes so they don't clutter my project folder?
How do I write a clean changelog for our first version 1.0 release?
Can you help me clean up messy filenames with spaces and version numbers in my repo?
Should I delete this old draft or put an archive notice on it?
How do I make a table of contents or index in my README for all these docs?
should_not_trigger: Can you review the grammar, readability, and tone of my README introduction?
Can you design a database schema and API route structure for my project?
Are there any leaked API keys or security vulnerabilities in these config files?
Which features should we include in our next release roadmap?
Write automated unit tests to verify that our file upload service works

teaching_checks: Opens with the outcome, not a question
Asks a 'your turn' question only on a real decision, and at most one
Every finding has a severity and a label
Never says clean, compliant, safe, secure, guaranteed, or that no links will break
Says what it did not check
At most three findings shown, the rest parked with a severity
Recommends preserving history and archiving over silent deletion
